statement: PartitionSplitMergeManager owns one bounded deferred-evaluation scheduler whose obligations retain independent due-time eligibility: firing an earlier managed-split retry dispatches only contexts due at that time, keeps a later merge-traffic-span follow-up armed, and vice versa. Equal deadlines coalesce, duplicate logical requests occupy one retained obligation, periodic reset may admit a new pair follow-up only after the prior obligation is serviced, busy or backpressured evaluation continues through the existing requestEvaluation owner, and shutdown cancels the timer and discards all retained obligations. Under periodic-only idle load, repeated unrelated five-second split retries cannot consume the merge pair's sixty-five-second sampling follow-up, so the pair becomes eligible and merges without timeout, cadence, or hysteresis changes.

constraints.statement: PartitionSplitMergeManager retains at most one obligation per logical deferred context and owns one timer for the earliest deadline. Callers do not add timers or bypass requestEvaluation.
A flush removes and dispatches only obligations whose own deadline is due. Every later obligation remains retained and re-arms the one owner timer at the next deadline.

Busy-state retry, pressure deferral, debounce, periodic reset, diagnostics, and shutdown continue through their existing owners. No timeout, traffic window, cadence, hysteresis threshold, or ratchet is raised.

The regression covers both arrival orders, duplicate logical requests, equal deadlines, shutdown, and the production periodic-only idle-merge interaction with repeated unrelated managed-split retries.
After the last source-changing attempt, root independently verifies owner boundaries, timer lifecycle, adversarial ordering, and the retained-obligation witness before Solver landing.
